BiblicalUsage: Og was the king of Bashan, a giant of the Amorites, defeated by Moses before Israel crossed the Jordan. His bedstead was of iron, nine cubits long, and his land was given to the half tribe of Manasseh.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Og is the proof that no enemy is too big for God: his bed was thirteen feet long, and Israel took his land and gave it to the tribes.
RelatedEvents: The Defeat of Sihon and Og
